cards.name: Uncle FrizzleBob's Federal Reserve Secret
cards.power: Pattern Recognition: If opponents read the fine print on their money, draw 2 cards.
cards.lore: 100 years of debt slavery disguised as economic stability. Cut out these cards, play the game, and watch the illusion burn.
cards.gradeReason: Perfect thesis card—rabbit mascot plus money paranoia is instant table fuel.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: conspiracy comic. Subject: rabbit exposing burning dollar bill. Mood: gleeful revelation.

cards.name: The Creature from the Fed
cards.power: Spawn: Take 1 labor token from every player turn. You are the Creature.
cards.lore: It’s not Federal, and there is no Reserve. A private banking cartel that bought the right to print your money.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus-fed monster is iconic and brutally clear as a villain opener.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: horror satire comic. Subject: octopus around federal reserve temple. Mood: predatory control.

cards.name: Fiat Conjuring
cards.power: Generate 10 debt tokens from nothing. Laugh. Carry inflation.

cards.gradeReason: Wizard fox money magic lands instantly—clean satire and strong utility.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: magical satire comic. Subject: fox magician printing glowing money. Mood: smug illusion.

cards.name: Economic Jargon

cards.gradeReason: Owl jargon prison is strong flavor, though more support than star.

cards.name: Bank of England (1694)
cards.power: Loan your opponent 5 tokens. Demand 10 tokens back.

cards.gradeReason: Historical lion banker gives the deck real teeth—excellent foundation card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: historical comic. Subject: lion banker with royal gold. Mood: origin of corruption.

cards.name: Fractional Reserve Illusion

cards.gradeReason: Pyramid scam visual is perfect and mechanically nasty.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: symbolic comic. Subject: glowing pyramid of fake gold. Mood: illusion of wealth.

cards.name: Bank of North America (1781)
cards.power: I print war. Every dollar you use funds my next one.
cards.lore: The missing founding. First private U.S. bank before the Constitution. War needed funding before freedom.
cards.gradeReason: Revolutionary skunk banker is great lore glue, slightly less punchy mechanically.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: colonial satire comic. Subject: skunk banker with cannon and chest. Mood: funded revolution.

cards.name: Alexander Hamilton's Ghost

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghostly political comic. Subject: ghost fox with constitution papers. Mood: spectral ambition.

cards.name: First Bank of the U.S.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: financial satire comic. Subject: eagle hatching money egg. Mood: predatory finance.

## QA

qa.verdict: This deck is conspiracy economics turned into a wrestling promo against central banking, and somehow it absolutely works. The best cards—The Creature from the Fed, Quantitative Easing, Kayfabizarro Anarchy—translate abstract monetary systems into clean table violence and unforgettable imagery. Some mid-deck wording gets OCR-chaotic enough to sound like prophecy from a haunted accountant, but honestly that improves the vibe. Table-ready? Yes. Hide it near your uncle before Thanksgiving and let destiny handle the rest.

urgent: Clean several OCR-heavy lines in the debt mechanics section for smoother readability
quickWins: Standardize naming between historical institutions and symbolic economy cards
Tighten Economic Jargon and Un-Printable Math for clearer gameplay text
niceToHave: Slightly sharpen Ellen Brown / public banking section for stronger late-game contrast

notes: Cover page is decorative only and not counted as a card page. Several late-deck resistance cards intentionally pivot from conspiracy satire into practical counter-economy philosophy, and that tonal shift should be preserved. This deck works best when the powers stay short, cruel, and financially insulting.
marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: FEDERAL KAYFABE – The Private Cartel That Owns the Money Printer (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

A private club prints the dollars you borrow, then bills you interest for the privilege of using them.

Here is the move, run slowly so you can watch the hands. A handful of private banks get chartered as a public-sounding agency in 1913. They conjure money from a keystroke, lend it to the government at interest, and let a century of quiet inflation skim your wages while the result gets called stable. When the machine breaks, the same people who built it sign the bailouts and apologize on their way out the door. The cartel is the opponent, and the cartel has never once had to wrestle in the open.

Federal Kayfabe racks that whole apparatus as a rogues' gallery you can cut out and pin: sixty cards, Jekyll Island to quantitative easing, dealt straight into your hands. You take a card, you sell its con with a straight face, and the table rules whether the racket holds or gets exposed mid-sentence. Social Story Wrestling for anyone who ever noticed the printer never runs for them.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Federal Kayfabe Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring Fiat Conjuring, The Creature from the Fed, and Bernanke's Hollow Apology.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No compound-interest homework, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the house rule that every power stays short, cruel, and financially insulting.
- The Counter-Economy Turn: the late cards stop mocking the cartel and start arming against it, from Quantitative Easing run as a finishing move to Kayfabizarro Anarchy, where the table walks out of the casino entirely.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
A swindle survives on nobody being willing to perform it out loud, and the central bank is the longest-running act on the bill. I draw these cards to make the performance cheap and impossible to ignore. Broke? Enter "0" and take it, which is the only honest opening price for a deck about a rigged money supply. Print it, cut it, leave the cards places. Want to support the craft? Every coin goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards. Share and remix freely under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
